lesson.title: Data all around the school
lesson.subtitle: Facts we record, tables, and the rules that make them count

video.title: Data all around the school
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Register; Notebooks; WhatsApp; Where?. Amina beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The district asked me a simple question: how many of my pupils walk more than thirty minutes to school? The answer is somewhere. In my register, two notebooks and a WhatsApp chat!

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: the data your school already keeps, and how to put it in a table a computer can use.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Who came today; A pupil's mark; How much rain fell; Written down to use later.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Data are facts we record. Who came today. A pupil's mark. How much rain fell. Each one is something we noticed, written down so we can use it later.

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Register; Mark book; Library cards; Rain gauge.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Your school is full of data
scenes.narration: Your school is full of data. The register, the mark book, library cards, the rain gauge in the garden. Most of it sits on paper, or in a sheet only one person can open.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Row: one thing; Column: one fact; Cell: one value.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A table keeps data in rows and columns. Each row is one thing: a pupil, a day or a reading. Each column is one fact about it, like a name or a mark. Where they meet is a cell.

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Numbers: 14, 25 min; Categories: 5B, walks; Dates: 2 March; Text: comments.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Values come in kinds. Numbers, like marks or minutes, can be added up. Categories, like a class or how you travel, can be counted. Dates and free text need their own care.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Each row: a pupil; Each column: a day; P present, A absent; Easy to count.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: You already use a table every morning. In the register, each row is a pupil and each column is a day. Each cell holds one letter: P for present, A for absent. Simple, and easy to count.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! One cell in my mark sheet says fourteen slash seventeen: a pupil's maths and science marks together. What's wrong with it?

scenes.visual: Numbered steps: One row per thing; One column per fact; One value per cell; No totals inside the data.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Two facts in one cell: the computer sees text, and can't add it up. Tidy tables follow simple rules. One row per thing. One column per fact. One value per cell, and no total rows among the pupils.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Class written once, blanks below; A Total row among the pupils; Two marks in one cell; People read it; computers miscount.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here's how a sheet goes wrong. The class is written once, then left blank below. A Total row sits between the classes. Two marks share one cell. People read it easily, but a computer counts it wrong.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: A messy sheet; Tap a fix; Answers turn right.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, Mr Bello's mark sheet looks fine, but the computer gets three questions wrong. Tap one fix at a time and watch its answers. Which fix turns the most answers right?

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. I'm making a table of how my pupils come to school, and how long it takes. What should one row be?

scenes.visual: Summary card: Data: facts we record; Rows are things, columns are facts; One value per cell; Tidy tables count right. Takeaway bar: Tidy it once, and every count comes out right.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: One pupil per row, with columns for how they travel and the minutes it takes. Remember: data are facts we record. A table keeps them in rows and columns. And a tidy table is one a computer can count.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A table on the board; One row per pupil, by number; Columns: travel, minutes; Count together. Amina beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: draw a table on the board. One row for each pupil, by number, not by name. Columns for how they come to school, and the minutes it takes. Then count together: how many walk more than thirty minutes?

checkpoints.prompt: A cell says “14 / 17”: a pupil's maths and science marks. What's the problem?

options.text: Two facts in one cell, so the computer sees text
The marks should be out of 100

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — two facts share one cell, so it's text to a computer. Split it into a maths column and a science column.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — people can read it, but a computer sees “14 / 17” as text and can't add it up. One value per cell.

checkpoints.prompt: A table of how pupils come to school and how long it takes: what should one row be?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the table is about pupils, so one row per pupil, with a column for how they travel and one for the minutes.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — each row is one thing the table is about: here, one pupil. How they travel and the minutes are columns.
